import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1090

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1090](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1090)
- [Er75f] Erdős, Paul, *On some problems of elementary and combinatorial geometry*. Ann. Mat. Pura Appl. (4) (1975), 99-108.
-/

namespace Erdos1090

/--
Let $k\geq 3$. Does there exist a finite set $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ such that, in any $2$-colouring of $A$, there exists a line which contains at least $k$ points from $A$, and all the points of $A$ on the line have the same colour?

Erdős [Er75f] says Graham and Selfridge proved the answer is yes when $k=3$. Hunter has observed that, for sufficiently large $n$, a generic projection of $[k]^n$ into $\mathbb{R}^2$ has this property, by the Hales-Jewett theorem.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos1090.lean"]
theorem erdos_1090 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (k : ℕ), ∀ (hk : 3 ≤ k),
    ∃ (A : Finset (Fin 2 → ℝ)), ∀ (C : A → Fin 2),
      ∃ (S : Finset (Fin 2 → ℝ)), ∃ (hSA : S ⊆ A),
        Collinear ℝ (S : Set (Fin 2 → ℝ)) ∧ S.card ≥ k ∧
          (∀ y ∈ A, y ∈ affineSpan ℝ (S : Set (Fin 2 → ℝ)) → y ∈ S) ∧
          ∃ c, ∀ x (hx : x ∈ S), C ⟨x, hSA hx⟩ = c := by
  sorry

end Erdos1090

reformulations.difference: Lean quantifies a collinear finset S ⊆ A satisfying an affine-span exhaustion condition, rather than explicitly quantifying a line. It also restricts the primary paper’s “for every k” to k ≥ 3.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Since S.card ≥ k ≥ 3, S contains two distinct points p and q. Collinear.affineSpan_eq_of_ne identifies affineSpan(S) with the genuine line through p and q. The exhaustion condition, together with S ⊆ A and S ⊆ affineSpan(S), gives S = A ∩ affineSpan(S). Thus the cardinality and coloring clauses say exactly that this line contains at least k points of A and all points of A on it have one color. Conversely, given such a line L, take S = A.filter (· ∈ L); its affine span is contained in L, so exhaustion and the other clauses follow. The restriction k ≥ 3 is harmless: a witness for max(k,3) also works for k. Pointwise and quantified equivalences, including the threshold equivalence, were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using any sorry-backed theorem.

sources_consulted: Paul Erdős, On Some Problems of Elementary and Combinatorial Geometry, Ann. Mat. Pura Appl. (4) 103 (1975), 99–108, §4, p. 106: https://renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1975-25.pdf

review.notes:
Checked the sole declaration, its definitions, quantifier dependencies, answer polarity, and boundary cases. Empty or singleton collinear sets cannot be witnesses; more generally every witness forces k ≤ A.card. The coloring type is inhabited even for empty A, so its universal quantifier is not vacuous.

The linked external strict theorem states exactly the required conclusion for each k ≥ 3. A scratch-only copy with five tactic compatibility adjustments from Lean/Mathlib 4.29.1 to 4.33.1 compiled successfully; its printed axioms are only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. This supports answer(True), research solved, and the formal_proof record.

Limitation: erdosproblems.com returned Cloudflare HTTP 403 despite descriptive User-Agent headers; its current wording, remarks, and metadata could not be read directly. Mathematical faithfulness was settled against the cited primary paper, and the affirmative solution was checked through the linked proof. Review artifacts are in /workspace/review/; the reviewed file remains identical to the committed file.
